content.title: About
content.content: Potato bread is a baked product in which boiled or mashed potato is incorporated into the dough. The potato makes the crumb softer, adds moisture and a subtle sweet flavor. It is often used in dietetic cooking because the potato reduces gluten content and boosts nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first potato‑bread recipe appeared in the 19th century in Europe as a way to use leftover boiled potatoes.
Potato bread stays fresh longer than regular wheat bread thanks to its higher moisture content.
In some countries, such as Poland, potato bread is a traditional holiday food.
Adding potato reduces the amount of starch from flour, making the loaf easier to digest.
Potato bread usually has a lighter crust and a softer crumb.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Potatoes contain vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Potato bread provides additional dietary fiber that aids regular digestion.

items.title: Lower glycemic index than plain white bread
items.content: The presence of potato can lower the overall glycemic index, making it more suitable for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to potatoes, experiencing skin reactions or digestive upset.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Although potato reduces gluten, the loaf still contains wheat flour and is not suitable for celiac disease.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added during preparation; individuals with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: If potato‑enriched dough is left at room temperature too long, bacterial growth can occur, so follow proper storage times and conditions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Potato bread can be enjoyed like regular bread: toasted, with butter, cheese, pâté, or as a base for sandwiches. It is also used for croutons, casseroles, and as a side for soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight bag or container. For longer freshness keep it in the refrigerator, where it stays soft for 5–7 days. Freeze in freezer‑safe bags if you need to keep it for more than a week.
